about: One entry per target engine. `status` is set by run.py: `working` only after the real model produced Russian audio files in this environment. Every claim cites where it was verified. Weights for the neural engines were fetched from modelscope.cn and verified byte-for-byte (SHA-256) against the official Hugging Face repo at the pinned revision (fetch_models.py; huggingface.co's large-file CDNs are refused by this environment's network policy).

engines.label: RHVoice
engines.commercial_review: yes — 9 of the 14 Russian voices are CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0 (non-commercial); aleksandr-hq is CC-BY-SA-4.0; the rest LGPL-2.1+ per the Debian copyright file.
engines.stress_handling: Honors U+0301: «пи́шу»/«бе́рега» change the audio; a mark matching default stress gives byte-identical audio (measured in phase 1). Deterministic.

engines.label: Piper

voices.ru-irinia-medium: GPLv2 per the voice's MODEL_CARD (dataset: RHVoice); fine-tuned from the en_US lessac medium voice

engines.commercial_review: yes — voice is GPLv2 per its model card and is a fine-tune of the lessac voice, whose dataset terms need separate review.
engines.partial_blocker: The other Russian Piper voices (ru_RU-denis/dmitri/ruslan/irina-medium) are hosted only on huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices — CONNECT 403 here. Only ru-irinia-medium is available as a GitHub release asset.
engines.stress_handling: espeak-ng ignores U+0301 and mis-stresses words containing it (dictionary miss → letter rules): «перейти́» → pʲirʲˈejtʲi vs unmarked pʲirʲijtʲˈɪ (phase 1).

engines.label: XTTS v2
engines.model: coqui/XTTS-v2 @ 28ac75746581 (tag v2.0.1; identical files to v2.0.0) — model.pth sha256 a9bf08409cde…; NOT the newer v2.0.3 on main
engines.python_package: coqui-tts 0.27.5 (idiap fork) + transformers 4.57.6 + spacy 3.8.16 (needed by its sentence splitter), torch 2.6.0 CPU
engines.gpu_required: no — runs on CPU; GPU would only speed it up

license.model: Coqui Public Model License 1.0.0 — non-commercial use of the model AND its outputs only

voices.en_sample: reference clip from the CPML-licensed model repo

engines.commercial_review: yes — CPML forbids commercial use of the model and its outputs; Coqui (the licensor) has shut down, so a commercial license cannot be bought.
engines.voice: cloned from samples/en_sample.wav shipped in the model repo (the ModelScope mirror has no speakers_xtts.pth; no Russian sample exists in the repo)
engines.stress_handling: Tokenizer vocab has no U+0301: every mark becomes an [UNK] token and breaks the BPE split around it («за́мок» → за·[UNK]·мо·к vs «замок» → за·мо·к). Marks also count toward the 182-char Russian limit and can trigger sentence splitting (#22).
engines.network_notes: Weights: huggingface.co API reachable, but its LFS/Xet CDNs (us.aws.cdn.hf.co, cas-server.xethub.hf.co) are refused (CONNECT 403), so files came from modelscope.cn with SHA-256 verified against the HF revision. torch from PyPI (download.pytorch.org redirects to download-r2.pytorch.org, refused).

engines.label: Chatterbox Multilingual V3
engines.python_package: chatterbox-tts 0.1.7 from GitHub master @ 5de7a54 (has the V3 loader), transformers 5.2.0, torch 2.6.0 CPU
engines.gpu_required: no — runs on CPU; GPU would only speed it up

license.model: MIT (model card front matter, ResembleAI/chatterbox README.md)

voices.builtin: conds.pt, part of the MIT model repo

engines.commercial_review: light — MIT. Output carries Resemble's Perth imperceptible watermark by default.
engines.stress_handling: Vocab HAS a U+0301 token and the model is trained on stressed Russian: marks reach the model as their own tokens. The package would auto-stress Russian via an optional `russian_text_stresser` module, which is not a declared dependency and was not installable → skipped with a warning (recorded per synthesis). NFKD also splits й into и+U+0306.
engines.rate_support: none — no speed/duration control; slow items synthesized at default rate
engines.network_notes: Weights: huggingface.co API reachable, but its LFS/Xet CDNs (us.aws.cdn.hf.co, cas-server.xethub.hf.co) are refused (CONNECT 403), so files came from modelscope.cn with SHA-256 verified against the HF revision. torch from PyPI (download.pytorch.org redirects to download-r2.pytorch.org, refused).

license.model: Apache-2.0 (huggingface.co model card metadata; the ModelScope README has no license header)

voices.zero_shot_prompt: prompt clip from the Apache-2.0 repo

(Its wetext normalizer could not load here anyway: it downloads from www.modelscope.cn, refused.)

engines.label: MOSS-TTS-Nano
engines.adapter: engines/moss_nano.py (+ engines/moss_nano_worker.py in envs/moss-nano, repo tools/MOSS-TTS-Nano)
engines.model: OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-TTS-Nano-100M @ 44502f80dbf9 (0.1B, pytorch_model.bin 235 MB) + OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer-Nano @ 6aa02b01e445 (~20M, 85 MB); 48 kHz stereo output
engines.python_package: official repo OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano @ 8b7bcc9 (requirements.txt pins: torch 2.7.0, transformers 4.57.1, WeTextProcessing 1.2.0), float32 CPU
engines.voice: cloned from native-Russian FLEURS clips (references/references.json; Google FLEURS, CC-BY-4.0): ru_female_fleurs, ru_male_fleurs; the repo's built-in presets are Chinese/English/Japanese only

license.model: Apache-2.0 (model card front matter; same for MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer-Nano)

engines.commercial_review: light — Apache-2.0 model and code; reference clips are CC-BY-4.0 (attribution).
engines.rate_support: none — no speed control; slow items synthesized at default rate
engines.stress_handling: U+0301 survives the repo's text pipeline (robust cleanup + WeText) unchanged. It is NOT a SentencePiece vocab piece: byte fallback encodes each mark as the byte pair <0xCC><0x81>, so marks reach the model as bytes (no [UNK], no dropping). Measured: all marked sentence pairs give different audio; unmarked controls (#25, #28) are byte-identical across runs. Separate finding: with WeText ON (repo default), pure-Cyrillic text is routed to WeText's Chinese grammar — digits become Chinese numerals («3 бра́та» → «三 бра́та», «01.09.2026 в 14:30» → «二零二六年九月一日 в 十四点三十分»); the voice config '+no-wetext' turns it off.

engines.stress_handling: U+0301 survives the repo's text pipeline (robust cleanup + WeText) unchanged. It is NOT a SentencePiece vocab piece: byte fallback encodes each mark as the byte pair <0xCC><0x81>, so marks reach the model as bytes (no [UNK], no dropping). Measured: all marked sentence pairs give different audio; unmarked controls (#25, #28) are byte-identical across runs. Separate finding: with WeText ON (repo default), pure-Cyrillic text is routed to WeText's Chinese grammar — digits become Chinese numerals («3 бра́та» → «三 бра́та», «01.09.2026 в 14:30» → «二零二六年九月一日 в 十四点三十分»); the voice config '+no-wetext' turns it off. Same tokenizer and text pipeline in the ONNX path.

engines.label: F5-TTS Russian
engines.adapter: engines/f5_espeech.py (+ engines/f5_espeech_worker.py in envs/f5) — prepared, never ran
engines.model: intended: hotstone228/F5-TTS-Russian @ 4b9fcb51e68b (the only Russian checkpoint in F5-TTS SHARED.md; F5-TTS Base fine-tune, 813k steps, Common Voice 17 + Golos + SOVA + RESD) — fallback: ESpeech/ESpeech-TTS-1_RL-V2 @ f582b6e5897f (Russian F5-TTS, Apache-2.0)

license.model: hotstone228/F5-TTS-Russian: CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 per its model card (SHARED.md says cc-by-nc-4.0); ESpeech-TTS-1: Apache-2.0

engines.stress_handling: not measured (no weights). Static finding: both Russian vocabs contain U+0301 (index 1574, inherited from the base vocab) AND '+'; ESpeech's own pipeline writes stress as '+' before the vowel via ruaccent.

blocker.detail: No Russian F5-TTS checkpoint was obtainable here. hotstone228/F5-TTS-Russian: weights only on huggingface.co, whose large-file CDNs (us.aws.cdn.hf.co, cas-server.xethub.hf.co) are refused (CONNECT 403). ESpeech-TTS-1 (all variants) on modelscope.cn: every GET is redirected to cdn-lfs-cn-1.modelscope.cn, refused (403); the repo's Git-LFS batch API answers 'mirror→mirror loop detected'. ESpeech's auto-stress models (ruaccent/accentuator) are huggingface.co-only as well. No substitute (non-Russian) F5 model was used.
blocker.unblock: Allow us.aws.cdn.hf.co / cas-server.xethub.hf.co (Hugging Face) or cdn-lfs-cn-1.modelscope.cn, then: python3 fetch_models.py espeech-rlv2 vocos-mel-24khz && python3 run.py f5-espeech

engines.label: MOSS-TTS Local 1.7B
engines.model: OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-TTS-Local-Transformer @ 12aa734e4f11 (MossTTSLocal; Qwen3-1.7B backbone, 3.06B params total, bf16 6.1 GB) + OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer @ 3cd226ba2947 (1.77B params, fp32 7.1 GB)
engines.python_package: OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS @ 934d682 remote code; transformers 5.0.0 + torch 2.9.1 CPU (MOSS-TTS pyproject pins); separate envs/moss-local
engines.cpu_only: loads and synthesizes on CPU (smoke test) — but only in bf16, not the official fp32 CPU dtype
engines.gpu_required: effectively yes for practical use: RTF 13.9–17 on this 4-core CPU
engines.stress_handling: Qwen3 BPE keeps U+0301 as its own token (#04: 5 marks → 5 tokens). Smoke test: as-is 2.88 s audio vs stripped 2.48 s (same seed) — the marks changed the output. Only #04 was synthesized.
engines.voice: cloned from the native-Russian FLEURS female clip (references/references.json, CC-BY-4.0)

blocker.detail: Official CPU config (float32) needs ~19.4 GB for weights alone (3.06B-param model ×4 B + 1.77B-param fp32 codec) > 15.7 GB RAM, no swap — not attempted. Smoke test with the weights' stored dtypes (model bf16, codec fp32) worked: load 11.9 s (lazy mmap), RSS 12.1 GB during generation, RTF 13.85–17.01 (#04: 49.0 s for 2.88 s of audio). Full corpus (64 syntheses) not run: >1 h at ~79% of RAM in a non-official dtype — stopped after the smoke test as instructed.
blocker.unblock: A GPU (official bf16 path), or ≥ 24 GB RAM for the official fp32 CPU path.
